convention: This file carries POINTERS AND TRAPS, not retellings. A задача is cited by its section in PLAN.md or SPEC.md, never paraphrased here: a paraphrase is a second copy of the truth and it drifts (it already did once, for routing_lists). What belongs here instead: file and symbol pointers, measured facts, rejected shapes with their arguments, and the traps that cost the last passes time. Written down in full in implementation-notes.md, section 'doclint — утверждение документа о состоянии обязано опираться на исполнимое'.

citation_hygiene.rule: Every path, T/W number, policy name and git ref named in this file must exist. This is no longer a convention a human has to remember — `go run ./cmd/doclint .` checks it, and CI runs it as `go run ./cmd/doclint -git=false .`.
citation_hygiene.why_this_block_still_exists: It records what the check is FOR. Two consecutive passes cited 'Global Constraint 9, constraints.md' — a file that never existed in any branch — and the citation was what justified deferring a task that, when finally checked on its merits, cost one optional field and one wiring line. The rule that citation stood in for: a pass closes its own queue item and does not widen into neighbouring modules; where the correct shape does require changing another package, that is recorded in Deviations with an argument — it is not grounds to defer the task silently.
citation_hygiene.exceptions_list: docs/not-yet-written.md — the single list doclint reads. It goes red in BOTH directions: a line that has become unnecessary is a finding too, so the list cannot rot into a dumping ground.

notes.doclint: Fast. Runs in CI as `go run ./cmd/doclint -git=false .` — a checkout has neither the pass branches nor the full history, so the git half is off there and on locally.
notes.negcheck: runs every guard twice (with/without its policy) via `go test -count=1`; 43 policies as of this pass, ~20-35 min wall clock on this machine — this is expected, not a hang; don't rely on go test's cache. It needs permission to listen on loopback: a network-restricted sandbox creates false oracle defects. Per-task gate only needs the new policy's own guard under HOP_DISABLE=<name>; the controller runs the full one at the end.
notes.realtimelint: does not accept ./... as an argument — pass literally `.`
notes.l3_how_to_run: Build once, run under an unprivileged user namespace: `go test -c -o /tmp/l3.test ./internal/l3` then `HOP_L3=1 unshare -Urn /tmp/l3.test` (add `-test.v -test.run '<pattern>'` to scope it). This works without root — unshare -Urn grants CAP_NET_ADMIN inside the fresh netns. Reusing the built binary across repeated unshare invocations is much faster than `go test` per run.
notes.known_red_that_is_not_yours: go vet ./... is red at internal/engine/dialer.go (copylocks in xray-core's SocketConfig). `go run ./cmd/realtimelint .` is red with 3 hits in internal/dnstest/realserver_test.go. `gofmt -l ./internal` reports internal/l2/dns_test.go. All three predate these passes; the honest gate is 'no NEW findings', compared on the full output rather than the exit code.
